# A restart that arrives while a stage is running is DEFERRED, not refused: the
# daemon restarts itself the moment nothing is in flight. The guard still never
# interrupts anyone's run — waiting for idle satisfies that by construction — but
# "come back later" no longer means a human has to. One daemon sat a whole evening
# on an old binary because the lane never happened to be quiet when anyone looked.
env BREEZE_DIR=$WORK/state

exec breeze register identity a
cp stdout a.token
exec breeze apply -f pipeline.hcl --as a --token-file a.token

# Start a stage that outlives the restart request, then ask for the restart.
exec sh -c 'breeze start stage slow s abc --as a --token-file a.token >/dev/null 2>&1 &'
exec sleep 2
exec breeze restart daemon
stdout 'DEFERRED until idle'
stdout 'slow/s \(a\)'

# The stage was NOT interrupted: it finishes on its own and records success.
exec breeze wait stage slow s abc --timeout 30s
stdout 'succeeded'

# Idle now: within a sweep tick the daemon restarts itself, and the client sees
# the re-exec'd daemon rather than a dead socket.
exec sleep 7
exec breeze ping
stdout 'pong'

exec breeze stop

-- pipeline.hcl --
pipeline "slow" {
  stage "s" {
    type    = "command"
    timeout = "1m"
    command = ["/bin/sh", "-c", "sleep 6"]
  }
}
